transcript_tail.text:
Verified — and the answer is more interesting than expected: **there is no new session.** My `claude -r --fork-session` actually **reattached to and drove the existing cloud session itself.**

Evidence from the filesystem + cloud API:

| Signal | Before | After my run |
|---|---|---|
| Local transcript `b28ebd4b…jsonl` | 257 KB @ 18:56 | **384 KB @ 19:05** (appended, not a new file) |
| Cloud `last_event_at` | 01:56:15Z | **02:06:25Z** (just now) |
| Status | idle / connected | **running** / connected |
| Title | `[JOB] Dstrader docs` | **`[FF] #dstrader-docs website technical deep-dives`** (auto-retitled) |

So, directly answering you:

- **In the desktop app you will NOT see a brand-new chat.** You'll see the *same* session — the one that was "[JOB] Dstrader docs" — jump to the top, now marked **running**, retitled "[FF] #dstrader-docs website technical deep-dives", with my test turn in its history. It's the existing `cse_01KAWgmqDG6Tm8oQGYMzD18o` cloud session, which is exactly what the app lists.

- **Why:** that session was **`connected`** — a live remote-control/bridge worker was attached on this host. So resuming its local transcript drove the *live* cloud session rather than creating an isolated copy. `--fork-session` did **not** fork here (print mode kept `session_id: b28ebd4b…` and appended to the original).

**Correction to what I told you earlier:** I said the original was "unaffected either way." That was only true for the *code/files* (no writes, no commits). The **transcript and the cloud session were affected** — my turn was appended and the session got reactivated (idle→running). I should have caught that.

Implication worth knowing: **local `claude -r` against a *connected* bridge session ≠ a fresh session — it hijacks the live one.** To get a genuinely separate new session you'd resume one that's **disconnected**, or use `claude -p` with no `-r` (brand-new), or the cloud RemoteTrigger path.

Want me to confirm it settles back to `idle` (my one turn is done, so "running" should clear shortly), or leave it?

hmm, what other way we can start a sibling thread:
1) we create a new session but with the hsitory of the old
2) we tell the old sessino we moved work to the new session id

Right — what happened is the fork got hijacked **because that session was `connected`** (a live bridge worker owns it). The fix is to fork a session that's **`disconnected`** (no live worker to grab the prompt), or do a manual copy-fork. Let me lay out the clean mechanics for both of your ideas, then prove #1 safely.

**Your idea #1 — new session with the old history:** that's exactly what `--fork-session` is *supposed* to do: start from the old transcript but write to a **new** session id, leaving the original `.jsonl` untouched. It only failed last time because the target was live. Forking a disconnected one should produce a genuine new id.

**Your idea #2 — tell the old session work moved:** two flavors —
- *Non-executing marker (safe):* retitle the old session to `[MOVED→<newid>] …` via `titles set --id`. Pure metadata, visible in the app, doesn't wake the agent.
- *Executing note:* inject a turn (`claude -r <old> -p "work moved to <newid>, stop"`) — but that *runs* the old agent, same hijack risk. Prefer the retitle.

Let me find a **disconnected** session to fork safely and confirm the mechanics.

Found it — and a key discovery: there's a session **`[JOB] FF Docs`** (`cse_01DNt6FHiUuydk6msJV84Wec`, repo *job-search*, **idle/disconnected**). That's almost certainly the "FF DocS" you meant originally — it didn't show earlier because I filtered to the FamilyFund repo. And being **disconnected**, it's the safe one to fork.

Let me prove idea #1 on it: fork it, then verify a **new** session id/file was created and the **original is untouched**. (Fork is non-destructive — it only writes a new file. I'll hold the #2 retitle for your OK since that mutates the old session's visible title.)

`--fork-session` failed to fork **again** — and this time the session was *disconnected*, so connectivity wasn't the cause. Look: the original `c71abac2…jsonl` just grew (1,035,630 → 1,046,051 bytes, mtime → 19:13) and `session_id` came back as `c71abac2` (the original). So **`claude -r --fork-session -p` does not create a sibling in this CLI/print mode — it appends to the original.** (It also cost $0.63 because each turn re-caches the ~1 MB transcript.)

So the built-in fork isn't viable here. The reliable way to get "new session id + old history + original untouched" is a **manual copy-fork**: copy the transcript to a fresh uuid filename (rewriting the internal `sessionId`), then resume *that*. Let me prove it — zero risk to the original:

**Copy-fork works — idea #1 is solved.** Proof from the run:

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| New sibling session id | `8875f5ec-4714-4ec0-9ff2-e775f87903bd` (≠ original `c71abac2…`) |
| Carries old history | 280 lines copied, `sessionId` rewritten on all 280 |
| Resume reported its own new id | `8875f5ec…` ✅ (a genuine separate session, unlike `--fork-session`) |
| **Original untouched** | `1046051 bytes, mtime 19:13:18` — **identical before & after** ✅ |
| Copy grew from the turn | 1,076,148 → 1,088,091 bytes ✅ |

(`result: None` just means the $0.20 cap cut the turn off mid-reply — the ids/sizes still prove the mechanism.)

So: **`claude -r --fork-session -p` does NOT fork here (appends to original); a manual copy-to-new-uuid + resume DOES** — new id, full history, original intact.

**One caveat that decides your next step** (the lesson from your last question): this sibling `8875f5ec` is a **local uuid session** — it shows in the local `/resume` picker for that worktree, but **not** in the desktop app's cloud-session list. Only `cse_` cloud sessions show in the app, and there's **no exposed way to clone a cloud session's *history* into a new cloud session** (RemoteTrigger only makes empty-history cloud sessions). So a full-history sibling is inherently CLI-local; an app-visible sibling has to be a fresh cloud session seeded with a *summary* handoff instead.

That changes what idea #2's pointer should even say, so:
